title: Sita: Choosing the Forest
subtitle: A wife's argument against remaining in the palace

learningObjectives.text: What is her argument for going?

choice.author: Valmiki
choice.locator: Ayodhyakandam · Section XXVII; Ayodhyakandam · Section XXVII, normalized characters 955-1557
choice.excerpt: I shall go before thee, Oh Raghava, treading upon the thorns and prickly grass. Confident do thou take me with thee, Oh great hero, renouncing jealousy and indignation, like unto water left after drinking; there exists no sin in me that could justify forsaking. Unto woman is preferable under all circumtances the shade of her husband's feet to the tops of a palace, the celestial car or excursion in the airy path.[131] I have been taught by my father and mother to follow my husband in all conditions of life; and I shall carry out now what I have been taught; I shall not abide by any other counsel.
choice.note: Verbatim English translation from Dutt. The Mahabharata volume is a condensed verse rendering; the Ramayana volume contains only the Balakandam and Ayodhyakandam.

narrativeBlocks.title: Stay, says the prince
narrativeBlocks.body: Rama tells Sita to remain in Ayodhya: the forest is no place for a princess — thorns, beasts, hunger, hardship. He paints the dangers vividly to spare her.

narrativeBlocks.title: 'I shall go before thee'
narrativeBlocks.body: Sita refuses the refusal: a wife's place is beside her husband, whatever the road. Her words stand among the epic's famous lines — she will go before him, treading down the thorns herself.

narrativeBlocks.title: The argument that wins
narrativeBlocks.body: Her case is devotion as duty: married to Rama, she shares his fortunes — palace or wilderness. A fourteen-year separation would be the harder path.

narrativeBlocks.title: Into the forest together
narrativeBlocks.body: Rama relents. Sita and his brother Lakshmana go with him — the trio of the forest years. The choice she insists on will place her in Ravana's path.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why the choice matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Her insistence is the hinge of the whole epic: had she stayed, no abduction, no war at Lanka. The Ramayana is built on a wife refusing to be left behind.

quiz.prompt: What is Sita's argument for going?
